title: Left Quillen adjunctions descend through left Bousfield localization
statement: Use model categories, functorial cofibrant replacements and Quillen adjunctions as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and simplicial model categories and derived mapping spaces as in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category and $\mathcal N$ any model category. Let $S$ be a small set of arrows of $\mathcal M$. A fibrant object $Z$ is $S$-local if every $(A\to B)\in S$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$. Assume a model structure $L_S\mathcal M$ exists with the original cofibrations and with weak equivalences exactly the maps inducing equivalences of derived mapping spaces into every fibrant $S$-local object; the derived mapping spaces in this definition use the original model structure. Let $F:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be a Quillen adjunction. If $FQ(s)$ is a weak equivalence for each $s\in S$, where $Q$ is a functorial cofibrant replacement in the original structure, then the same adjoint functors give a Quillen adjunction $F:L_S\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Proposition 3.3.18(1), printed p. 63. Simplicial source so homotopy function complexes use the displayed derived mapping-space formula; neither properness nor combinatoriality is needed once the localization exists, and no simpliciality of the target is assumed.

proof.text: Write $C,W$ for the original cofibrations and weak equivalences and $W_S$ for the displayed local equivalences. The mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies the derived mapping spaces with mapping spaces in the original infinity localization. Thus every original weak equivalence induces equivalences of derived mapping spaces into each fibrant $S$-local object, so $W\subseteq W_S$. The original and localized trivial fibrations are both exactly the arrows with the right lifting property against $C$, by the model weak factorization system $(C,F\cap W)$ and the equality of cofibrations. In particular the two classes of trivial fibrations coincide. The underlying adjunction $F\dashv U$ is unchanged because the underlying categories are unchanged.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.3(1) and the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 3.3.18(1), printed pp. 58,63; equality of trivial fibrations written out from the model axioms Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix a fibrant $Y\in\mathcal N$. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the original right Quillen functor $U$ preserves fibrations and therefore $UY$ is fibrant: $U$ preserves the terminal object and the fibration $Y\to1$. Let $q_{\mathcal M},q_{\mathcal N}$ denote original infinity localizations. The same cited node gives the derived adjunction and its formula $\mathbf L F(q_{\mathcal M}A)=q_{\mathcal N}FQA$. For $s:A\to B$ in $S$, its natural mapping-space equivalence, together with [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], identifies the arrow $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}^h(B,UY)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}^h(A,UY)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal N_\infty}(q_{\mathcal N}FQB,q_{\mathcal N}Y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal N_\infty}(q_{\mathcal N}FQA,q_{\mathcal N}Y)$. Here $\mathbf R U(q_{\mathcal N}Y)$ is represented by $UY$ because $Y$ is already fibrant (or use $UY\to UTY$, a weak equivalence between fibrant objects by the same cited node). By hypothesis $FQ(s)$ is a weak equivalence, so its image under $q_{\mathcal N}$ is an equivalence and this precomposition map is an equivalence. Thus $UY$ is $S$-local. This uses no simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal N$ or of the adjunction.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.6(1), implication (b) to (c), printed pp. 49-50, used in Proposition 3.3.18(1); derived mapping-space adjunction supplies the comparison for the one chosen functorial replacement Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Let $p:X\to Y$ be a fibration of $\mathcal N$ with $X,Y$ fibrant. The original Quillen adjunction preserves fibrations on the right by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], so $Up:UX\to UY$ is a fibration in $\mathcal M$. Step 2 shows that both endpoints are fibrant $S$-local objects. Apply [lem-coef-bousfield-local-fibrations] to the given model structure $L_S\mathcal M$: its hypotheses are exactly the fixed-cofibration and original-derived-mapping-space description in the item. It follows that $Up$ is a fibration in $L_S\mathcal M$.

source.place: Last paragraph of the proof of Proposition 3.3.18(1), using Proposition 3.3.16(1), printed p. 63 Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For an arbitrary trivial fibration $p$ of $\mathcal N$, with no fibrancy restriction on its endpoints, [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] says $Up$ is an original trivial fibration. Step 1 identifies it with a trivial fibration of $L_S\mathcal M$. Hence $U:\mathcal N\to L_S\mathcal M$ preserves all trivial fibrations and, by Step 3, all fibrations between fibrant objects. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-fibrant-test] with $\mathcal A=L_S\mathcal M$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal N$, $L=F$, $R=U$. The same adjoint functors are a Quillen pair, as required.

source.place: First paragraph of the proof of Proposition 3.3.18(1), applying Proposition 8.5.4(3) to (1), printed pp. 63,153-155 Read online; not archived in literature/.
